description: Salzburg Research publishes SIT-PET, time-resolved road-user trajectories and post-encroachment-time interaction events at one signalized intersection in Salzburg, Austria. The deposit includes vehicle, pedestrian and two-wheeler attributes, signal states, weather observations and eight predefined conflict scenarios. The article describes two years of collection, but only a representative six-month temporal subset is public; the full series is available from the authors on request. The Zenodo concept DOI cited by the article resolves to a named version page, which lists ZIP archives and README or schema files. The public subset is free under CC BY 4.0. These observations can calibrate microscopic traffic and pedestrian simulations or test surrogate-safety rules. Coverage is limited to one junction. PET outputs are raw calculations without a single criticality threshold, so users must choose event definitions. The archives and Python examples were not downloaded or executed. No directly related catalogue dataset was identified.
name: Salzburg Intersection Trajectory and PET Interaction Dataset (SIT-PET)
